entities.summary:
Iago ab Idwal ap Meurig was a King of Gwynedd and of Powys, reigning from 1018 to 1039. Born around 1000, he was the son of Idwal ap Meurig and succeeded his father as King of Gwynedd and Powys. Iago ab Idwal ap Meurig played a significant role in the politics of medieval Wales, forming alliances with neighboring kingdoms and maintaining the independence of Gwynedd and Powys. He died in 1039, succeeded by his son Llywelyn ap Iago.

Iago ab Idwal ap Meurig's reign was marked by his efforts to strengthen the Welsh monarchy and resist the influence of the English crown. He was also known for his military campaigns against the English and the Vikings, which helped to secure the borders of Gwynedd and Powys. Iago ab Idwal ap Meurig's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, with his descendants playing a crucial role in the history of Wales and Scotland.

The impact of Iago ab Idwal ap Meurig's reign can still be felt today, with the survival of Welsh culture and language in part due to his efforts to preserve the autonomy of Gwynedd and Powys. His reign also provides a window into the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized medieval Welsh politics.

Iago ab Idwal ap Meurig was a key figure in the politics of medieval Wales, and his legacy continues to be studied by historians today.
